what_could_not_migrate: Per-claim editorial state. Every row reads NOT-RECORDED.
why: No register records whether a given claim row was adversarially reviewed. The method notes in 04-AUDITS/ record that a UNIT was reviewed; a unit is not a row, and expanding a unit-level review into 183 per-row REVIEWED-ACCEPTED values would assert something no reviewer said.
retained_unchanged: yes - nothing was written into the dimension
effect_if_ignored: A reader could take NOT-RECORDED for 'not reviewed'. Several of these registers HAVE been through adversarial review; the register just cannot say which rows.
needed_to_resolve: A decision on whether editorial state is recorded per claim or per unit, and if per unit, a unit register to join on.

what_could_not_migrate: The source_id cell writes a span as prose: 'SRC-053 to SRC-058'.
why: The span is unambiguous and the join expands it, but rewriting the register cell would edit a row another unit wrote to suit a tool.
retained_unchanged: yes - the register cell is untouched; the six expanded join rows carry RANGE-EXPANDED-FROM-PROSE-CELL in notes
effect_if_ignored: The join is right and the mirror is prose; a future reader diffing the two will meet the discrepancy without explanation.
needed_to_resolve: Owner confirmation that SRC-053 to SRC-058 means those six ids and no others, then a one-line edit to the register cell by the unit that owns it.

what_could_not_migrate: Whether a row records a RETRIEVAL as distinct from a PROBE.
why: access_status uses VERIFIED for 65 rows and RETRIEVED for 4, and no document defines the difference. Some VERIFIED rows record a probe that FAILED (SRC-002, monthly limit reached; SRC-004, token expired), so VERIFIED cannot be read as 'retrieved'. Collapsing the two would destroy a distinction the ledger draws; inventing a retrieval_status from retrieval_capable would assert an event from a capability.
retained_unchanged: yes - access_status is untouched; access_status_class keeps PROBE-VERIFIED and RETRIEVED as separate closed values
effect_if_ignored: No machine check can tell a source that was opened from a source that was merely reachable.
needed_to_resolve: D-042 already asks whether reachability is a timestamped probe rather than a standing property. Answering it fixes this.

what_could_not_migrate: Publication state for rows whose supports_page names a page without a '(proposed)' marker.
why: A page existing is not evidence that this claim is published on it, and this repository cannot see the live site's content. Reading NOT-RECORDED as 'private' would be equally an invention.
effect_if_ignored: 279 rows read PROPOSED and 435 read NOT-RECORDED, and the second number is not a count of unpublished claims.
needed_to_resolve: A generated claim-to-route projection from melakeela/site, which is D-052.

what_could_not_migrate: The current_site_coverage and existing_route cells, which all read NOT ESTABLISHED.
why: The route inventory now exists and has been read (SRC-089, melakeela/site SITE-INVENTORY.md at e6b6b67, 133 root HTML files). Mapping 133 routes onto 89 backlog titles is a new editorial taxonomy, not an audit finding, and guessing it would produce the complete-looking unsourced CSV that D-014 and constitution section 1 exist to prevent.
retained_unchanged: yes - the sentinel is corrected to say where the inventory does exist, and nothing else
effect_if_ignored: Every backlog row still says coverage is unestablished, which is now true only of the mapping and not of the inventory.
needed_to_resolve: D-052: who owns the route-to-backlog mapping, and whether ambiguous rows go to owner review rather than a forced primary category.

what_could_not_migrate: A single eligibility authority. Both registers gate hypotheses; HYP-E-000 to HYP-E-009 and E-1 to E-11 are not mapped row for row.
why: Naming one canonical would retire the other's gate verdicts by clerical act. The two are related but their row sets differ and no crosswalk exists.
retained_unchanged: yes - both registers are untouched and both feed CLAIM-STATUS.csv
effect_if_ignored: Two eligibility authorities can disagree about the same hypothesis and nothing detects it.
needed_to_resolve: A row-for-row crosswalk, then D-053. The underlying question - whether the mandated registers accumulate under one name or split per domain - is D-036 and D-039, which are the same question at two identifiers.

what_could_not_migrate: A dependency row with only one side: source_b is empty.
why: The row records that a classification depends on a source, not that two sources depend on each other. The two-column schema cannot express it and changing the schema would rewrite the register.
effect_if_ignored: The row contributes no edge to the independence graph, so the graph is missing whatever it was meant to record.
needed_to_resolve: The unit that wrote DEP-007 states the second side, or the row is reclassified as something other than a dependency.

what_could_not_migrate: Nothing was migrated. This records a measurement the migration made visible.
why: 98 of 183 VERIFIED claims rest on sources that all fall in ONE independence group, so nothing behind them is shown to be independent of anything else behind them. CLAUDE.md caps single-source claims at PROVISIONAL. Demoting 98 rows mechanically would be rewriting research findings to satisfy a tool, and several are corpus measurements that are legitimately VERIFIED as counts over one corpus.
retained_unchanged: yes - no row was demoted and no row was promoted
effect_if_ignored: A reader may take 183 VERIFIED claims as 183 independently corroborated ones. They are not.
needed_to_resolve: D-051: whether a single independence group caps a claim at PROVISIONAL, or whether a measurement over one corpus is exempt and says so in its own row.

what_could_not_migrate: The link from a HOLD row to the hold that blocks it. Seven rows carry status HOLD and name no HOLD- file anywhere in the row.
why: CLAUDE.md requires a HOLD claim to be recorded in 05-HOLDS/ and six hold files exist, but no register carries a column for the link. This is a schema gap, not a defect in the rows: the rows are honest about being blocked. Choosing which hold blocks HYP-E-006 or E-2 is a judgement about someone else's row, and for E-3 the sources it names (SRC-037, SRC-040, SRC-041) appear in two hold files, so even the mechanical reading is ambiguous.
effect_if_ignored: A held claim cannot be traced to what would unblock it without reading prose, and the validator can only report the gap rather than enforce the link.
needed_to_resolve: A blocked_by_hold column on the eligibility registers, populated by the unit that owns each row. Queued as RA-019.
